Subjective:
- Current issues/reason for visit:
  - New swelling over left elbow noticed about 1 week ago.
  - Swelling is non-painful; feels slightly warm; patient perceives fluid within the area.
  - Full range of motion preserved; no functional limitation.
  - No preceding trauma or injury; no prior similar episodes.
- Past medical history:
  - Osteoarthritis diagnosed by GP a few years ago (site(s) not specified).
  - No known rheumatologic family history (patient unsure).

Objective:
- Examination (video consultation; left elbow):
  - Visible localized swelling around the tip/adjacent area of the left elbow.
  - Patient reports area is warmer than surrounding skin.
  - Patient reports no significant tenderness at the tip of the elbow; mild tenderness/“weird” sensation adjacent to the swelling.
  - Skin over tip of elbow noted as dry on video.
  - Full active range of motion of the left elbow.
  - No redness was reported or documented during the exam.
- Investigations:
  - None completed yet.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left elbow swelling:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Left elbow bursitis.
   - Differential diagnosis (as discussed): Septic arthritis, gout, inflammatory/rheumatologic disease.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Blood tests: inflammatory markers, infection screening, rheumatologic antibodies, gout screen. Blood test forms to be mailed; results expected ~5–6 days after sampling.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily; route not documented. Take after food; stop if heartburn occurs. Over-the-counter.
     - General advice: Monitor for worsening symptoms.
   - Safety net:
     - Seek urgent assessment if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads/increases (concern for acute infection).
   - Follow-up:
     - Arrange follow-up (video/phone or in-person) after blood tests are completed to review results and reassess the joint.
